integrity.notes: doit.py test-integrity exit 0. Diff vs base 0ebb31a: hand.ts only exports fullBetTarget/BetContext and narrows parameter types; legalActions uses fullBetTarget (same expression). action-bar.ts adds the unit/all-in wording and isShortAllIn. There is no recognition of test inputs, no hard-coded expected values and no mocks of the unit under test. Test support changes (a stacks override, four scene constants) are test-only. items.evidence: The named test passes and asserts betCount 4, currentBet 16 and the rendered enabled texts exactly ['Fold','Call $4']. The holdout's rendered bar on the same hand gave ['Fold','Call $4']. The browser capped-flop scene gave the same, and the live app showed Fold + Call $4 capped bars.

The test passes and asserts ['Fold','Call all-in $3'] plus the action {seat 5, call, 3}. The holdout reproduced it, and also preflop: $3 facing the $4 BB gives ['Fold','Call all-in $3'], and in chips 30 owed 40 gives 'Call all-in 30'. Killed by the 'call <=' and 'call never short' mutants.
The test asserts ['Fold','Call $4'] with stack $8. The holdout confirms the exact-stack plain label and no raise.

The test renders actionBar(view,'chips') and gets ['Fold','Call 40','Raise to 80'] with no '$'. The holdout also checked L-big stakes 1200/2400: ['Fold','Call 1200','Raise to 2400'] (no separator, D-4). The same state in default dollars uses '$'.

The test asserts stack 6, contribution 0, ['Fold','Call $4','Raise all-in to $6'] and the raise action amount 6. The holdout matched, and also got preflop $6 giving 'Raise all-in to $6', $8 giving plain 'Raise to $8', and the turn (big-bet unit) with $15 giving 'Raise all-in to $11' versus $20 giving 'Raise to $16'.
The test asserts ['Check','Bet all-in $3']. The holdout matched, and on the turn $6 behind gave ['Check','Bet all-in $6'].

The test asserts that the second-to-last action is seat 6 raise 5, seat 6 has stack 0, and the bar reads ['Fold','Call $1']. The holdout matched. It also showed a counted short all-in (raise to $6, at least half a bet over $4) moving the full target, giving ['Fold','Call $2','Raise to $10'].

The 100k property passes. Its D-5 oracle (an unlimited-stack legalActions) is independent of isShortAllIn and killed every labeling mutant. Separately, the judge's own oracle (first-principles counted-level replay; other seeds; a 6-stake set including 2000/4000 chips; random 2-10 seats; an aggression-biased policy) agreed on 60,015 decisions: callAllIn 8665, betAllIn 658, raiseAllIn 2449, capped 18901, notReopened 303, chip decisions 40885, preflop short calls 6998. One initial mismatch was the judge's oracle error: the engine keeps currentBet at the nominal big blind when the BB posts short, so 36 facing 40 is correctly 'Call all-in 36'.

The test asserts every listed actionLabel string. Holdout extras: 'Raise to 1200' (chips), {allIn:false} gives the plain label, {unit:'dollars',allIn:true} bet gives 'Bet all-in $6'. Killed by the unit-ignored and wording-order mutants.

The e2e test passes in Chromium and WebKit. It strips disabled, asserts the buttons are enabled, clicks normally, and data-action-count stays 5 with seat 6 to act. The judge's browser check also tried element.click(), a dispatched MouseEvent, Enter and Space on the stripped buttons: the count stayed 5 and seat 6 stayed to act in both engines.
The test calls ActionBar(...) and invokes each onClick, and the spy is never called. A second test with a disabled model carrying real actions is killed when onClick ignores model.enabled (mutation).
Both e2e tests pass in both engines (exact labels on 4 scenes, 44px, axe, no http requests). The judge's scene check reproduced the exact labels and at least 44x44 on every scene button.

The unit test asserts fullBetTarget = 8 on the AC#6 and AC#8 states, the A-1 edges ['Check','Bet $4'] / ['Fold','Call $4','Raise to $8'], isShortAllIn false for fold/check, and actionBar(view) equal to actionBar(view,'dollars'). The holdout repeated the edges and isShortAllIn raise 8 to false / 7 to true.
